Planner.ConfirmClear: Clear the queued sleep plan for the selected characters?

Rules.Title: Runyth Sleep — Rules
Rules.Intro: Define quality score boundaries and consequences. These are optional house rules, not D&D 5e core rules.
Rules.Outcomes: Consequences after a successful long rest

Help.Title: Runyth Sleep — Help
Help.Overview: The GM assigns one sleep plan per character. An actor can have only one pending plan. Plans are consumed after an ordinary completed D&D 5e long rest.
Help.StepOne: GM: open Configure Settings → Module Settings → Runyth Sleep → Open dashboard (or the bed button in Token Controls / character sheets). Find or select the character and click Set sleep.
Help.StepTwo: Choose bedding and environment, confirm the preview, then click Queue rest. For a group, select multiple characters in the dashboard and use Plan for selected.
Help.StepThree: Perform Long Rest from the character sheet as normal. Only queued plans produce consequences; an unplanned rest produces no additional effect. The dashboard shows the last result.
Help.Rules: Miserable and poor rests can add Exhaustion. Comfortable and excellent rests can grant temporary hit points. Both the thresholds and tier effects are customizable through Edit rules. Existing higher temporary hit points are never replaced.
Help.Authority: By default only GMs edit sleep rules. Under Permissions, a GM can delegate Edit sleeping rules to a trusted user or role. This does not grant Foundry-wide Configure Settings or control of other characters. Scene defaults and permission administration stay GM-only.
Help.Recovery: If the post-rest update fails, the pending plan remains queued. A GM may use the API retryApply(actor) from a macro or console after verifying that the long rest completed. A consumed plan is not reused.

ShelterExample.exposed: No overhead or wind protection: open field, exposed stone or sleeping directly under the sky.
ShelterExample.improvised: 15 minutes: throw leaves, branches or a loose tarp together for one night. Minimal protection.
ShelterExample.careful: 60 minutes: prepare a firm lean-to, tension a tarp carefully, add layered branches or a simple weatherbreak.
ShelterExample.indoor: Existing room, house, durable hut or robust long-term nomad tent, built to last months. Building one from scratch requires at least 24 hours.

Help.TimingHouseRules: The 15-minute, 60-minute and at-least-24-hour preparation times are Runyth Sleep campaign benchmarks, not timings mandated by the 2024 D&D core rules. The GM determines whether available materials and conditions allow construction.
Help.ScoringHeading: How the quality score determines consequences
Help.ScoringDetails: Add all seven modifiers: bedding + shelter + temperature + moisture + noise + safety + interruptions. The total determines one of five quality tiers. The ranges below reflect current configured thresholds. Each tier has separate, configurable saving-throw and temporary-HP rules.
Help.ConfiguredThresholds: A poor or miserable score does not automatically imply Exhaustion: the tier’s saving throw, DC, and save-success outcome control it. Likewise, a good score may trigger an HP roll rather than fixed HP. Edit Rules to inspect the precise DC and dice setup. Equipped armor is evaluated separately.
Help.SaveExplanation: Default: miserable sleep requires a CON save (base DC 15), poor sleep a CON save (base DC 12), both adjusted by configured scaling. Success negates the tier’s Exhaustion; failure applies the configured amount. Comfortable sleep rolls 1d4 + CON modifier (minimum 3 temporary HP); excellent sleep rolls 1d6 + 2 × CON modifier (minimum 5). Existing higher temporary HP is retained.

Settings.AutoApplyName: Apply consequences on completed long rest
Settings.AutoApplyHint: When off, queued plans remain pending until the GM manually applies or clears them.
Settings.CapHint: Default 5 avoids a sleep penalty alone causing Exhaustion 6 (death). Existing Exhaustion above the cap is preserved.
Settings.ChatHint: Control who sees the result message.
Settings.UnplannedHint: When no sleep plan exists, show a reminder after the rest, open the dashboard for the GM, or remain silent. No effects are applied without a plan.

Errors.GMOnly: Only the GM may perform this action.
Errors.NoActors: No character actors are available. Select a character token first.
Errors.ChatFailed: Sleep was applied, but the chat notification failed.
Errors.ApplyFailed: Sleeping consequences could not be applied. The plan was retained.
Errors.OpenFailed: Could not open the Runyth Sleep planner.
Errors.WrongSystem: Runyth Sleep requires the D&D 5e system.
Errors.PermissionDenied: You do not have permission to change the sleep plan for this character.
Errors.RulesUnavailable: A GM must initialize the dedicated sleeping-rules document before players can edit rules.
Errors.RulesChanged: Rules were changed by another editor. Reopen Edit Rules and try again.

Dashboard.Title: Runyth Sleep — Dashboard
Dashboard.Subtitle: Manage sleep quality and long-rest consequences across your characters.
Dashboard.SelectFirst: Select one or more characters first.
Dashboard.WorkflowDescription: GM: select one or more characters and assign sleeping conditions using Set sleep / Plan for selected. Then complete Long Rest on the character sheet. Consequences apply automatically only if a plan was queued.
Dashboard.PlanHint: View or change sleep conditions for the next long rest
Dashboard.MenuHint: Open the sleep dashboard for all characters, manage upcoming sleeping conditions and review outcomes.
Dashboard.NoPlanNotice: Long rest finished without a queued Runyth Sleep plan: no extra effects were applied. Open Runyth Sleep → Open dashboard in Module Settings, then set sleeping conditions before the next rest.
Dashboard.SidebarHint: Manage upcoming sleep conditions and long-rest consequences.
Dashboard.SceneHint: The Sleep Planner uses scene defaults when no plan is queued. The GM can choose and save them from the planner.
Dashboard.OverviewHint: Open Actors to find characters and manage queued long rests individually or in bulk.
Dashboard.SelectHint: Select characters to queue or clear their next long rest.
Dashboard.RulesHint: Rules are configured by the GM; sleeping conditions apply only after a completed long rest.
Dashboard.SettingsHint: Open Foundry Module Settings to change automation, Exhaustion cap, chat visibility, and unplanned-rest reminders.

Permissions.Title: Permissions
Permissions.Hint: Configure role minimums or user overrides. Rule editors may change only Runyth Sleep rules, using a dedicated permission-controlled rules document. Only a GM can grant permissions or manage world settings.
Permissions.planOwn: Queue or clear plans on owned characters
Permissions.OwnershipHint: Planning requires ownership of a character Actor. Rule editing is separately delegated: permitted users receive access only to the Runyth Sleep rules document; they cannot edit permissions, scene defaults, or unrelated world settings.
Permissions.UserHint: Override a role minimum for a specific user without changing other users. Inherit follows the minimum role.
Permissions.ResetConfirm: Reset all role minimums and user overrides to their defaults?
Permissions.editRules: Edit sleeping rules (including armor and DCs)

Mechanics.SaveHelp: On a successful roll, the specified reduction is applied to base Exhaustion. DC is calculated after a completed Long Rest, using severity and the actor's current stats. Native D&D 5e saving throws retain proficiency and active effects. Zero step disables a scaling term.
Mechanics.HPHelp: Dice add the selected ability modifier, proficiency bonus and optional level scaling. The base temporary HP is a minimum from older versions, not an additive bonus. Temporary HP does not stack. Only the highest value is kept.
Mechanics.Intro: House rules (not official D&D): configure each sleep grade independently. Saves are automatic after a completed Long Rest. Expand a grade to change DC scaling, saves, dice and bonuses. Results appear in chat and the actor’s latest sleep record.
Mechanics.ResetConfirm: Replace all custom sleep thresholds, tier consequences, saves, DC scaling and bonus rolls with the module defaults?

Fields.exhaustion: Exhaustion on failed save / without a save
Fields.qualityStep: Sleep-score points per DC step (0 = off)
Fields.exhaustionGain: DC change per current Exhaustion level
Fields.levelStep: Character levels per DC step (0 = off)

Armor.Title: Sleeping in Armor
Armor.Intro: 2024 core rules impose no sleeping-in-armor penalty. Xanathar’s Guide to Everything (older official optional rule) limits recovery after sleeping in medium/heavy armor without a save. Constitution saves are a configurable house rule, not official 2024 RAW.
Armor.ModeHint: Custom category profiles are used only in Constitution-save house rule mode. Equipped armor is checked when a Long Rest starts, even without a queued sleeping plan. Shields are ignored.

Preset.xanathar: Xanathar optional rule (25% spent Hit Dice, no Exhaustion recovery)

Armor.Failure: On failed save (or when save disabled)

Fields.preventRecovery: Prevent normal Long Rest Exhaustion reduction
Fields.hitDicePercent: Percent of spent Hit Dice recovered

Armor.ApplyFailed: Armor rest consequences could not be applied; see console and use GM recovery after resolving the error.
